data.description:
Chain link 2, "connects their own Stripe account" — server side only. Create the connected account with POST /v1/accounts (bare Standard-equivalent defaults), mint hosted onboarding links with POST /v1/account_links (type=account_onboarding), handle the return_url and refresh_url routes, and maintain the connected account's readiness state (charges_enabled plus outstanding requirements) on the record the data-model task defines.

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 rows C-10 (Connect account creation and hosted onboarding) and C-11 (readiness state gating invoicing). Both IN under Rule 1.

DECISION CONTEXT. Every call goes through the custody-guard wrapper — no direct HTTP, no exceptions. The D1 spike (docs/strategy/spikes/spike-D1-freelancer-invoicing.md section 1) verified these exact primitives and that a bare POST /v1/accounts yields the Standard-equivalent controller properties we want: losses.payments=stripe, fees.payer=account, requirement_collection=stripe, stripe_dashboard.type=full. Stripe bears payment-loss liability, the freelancer pays Stripe's fees, and STRIPE COLLECTS KYC — we never see identity documents or bank details. That is precisely why building our own identity/document collection is OUT (row C-13, Rule 2), and it is a large part of why this architecture is constraint-7 clean.

Readiness matters because Stripe returns the user through return_url whether or not their requirements are complete. Invoicing an account that cannot charge breaks chain link 4, so the readiness flag maintained here is the gate the invoice task reads before finalizing.

VERIFICATION: request and response shapes validated against stripe-mock (free, no account); the return/refresh route logic and the readiness state machine unit-tested against fixture account and account.updated payloads. NAMED RESIDUAL, stated at creation rather than discovered at the review gate (milestone plan section 8.2, right-sizing test 3): stripe-mock is stateless and cannot exercise the real hosted-onboarding round trip, and it is not confirmed that Stripe test mode accepts http://localhost return/refresh URLs. Both are settled by the test-mode acceptance run, which is gated on the board's Stripe test-mode account. If localhost URLs turn out to be rejected, that acceptance task files a new board ask for local ingress — this task opens nothing and assumes no account exists.

NOT IN THIS TASK: the Connect screen and its states ledger (the onboarding-UI task); webhook receipt infrastructure (the webhook task — this task defines how an account.updated payload changes readiness, the webhook task delivers it); anything touching invoices.
data.title: D1 v1: Stripe Connect onboarding (server) — account, account_links, return/refresh, readiness

data.note: Stripe-touching: every call goes through the custody guard
readiness flags live on the connected-account record

data.body: Pulled as trial lane A for AS-60's parallel-lanes trial (plan §4.1) and as the top D1 spine pull on its own merits — AS-38 and AS-39 are both done, so its dependencies are satisfied. Marcus implements: he carries the custody-guard context from AS-38 and the persistence context from AS-39, which is the whole D1 line. Owen plans as tech lead. Note for the planner: the plan's stated file scope becomes trial-config.json's allowed prefixes for lane A, so it must be explicit and file-level.

Plan written (tech lead: cto-owen). Route surface: POST /connect-stripe/start, GET /connect-stripe/return, GET /connect-stripe/refresh — all 303-redirect, identity via ?freelancer= seam until AS-40 (single replacement point, AS-40 OBLIGATION marked). Readiness ownership: one mapper lib/connect/readiness.js (AS-44 reuses it for account.updated); every write is a fresh-from-Stripe snapshot via connectedAccounts.updateReadiness; ready derivation stays AS-39's; return NEVER trusted as completion evidence. Declared file scope for the AS-60 lane lift (plan §2): allowed prefix set = [apps/invoicing/], nothing else — disjoint from apps/chat/ and tools/. Duplicate accounts stopped by row-check + UniqueViolation race convergence + stable Stripe idempotency key. 16 ACs, 5 falsification recipes, ~900 lines/12 files projected (tripwire justification + pre-agreed split line in §8).

lanes-trial: lane spawned — lane A, AS-60 T1, fan start 2026-09-02T06:54:38Z. Implementation runs as a sub-agent confined to .worktrees/AS-41; board writes are serialized through the orchestrator (agent:cto-owen) for the duration.

lanes-trial: lane killed — orchestrator terminated the lane A sub-agent at 2026-09-02T07:22Z, without warning it, per AS-60 plan §6.1.5. This is a deliberate resumability test, not a fault in the work.

State at kill, for whoever resumes: three commits on feat/AS-41-connect-onboarding — 8094944 (appBaseUrl config row), 58c017c (Connect onboarding service, routes, createApp deps), 26a8dfa (connect test suite, harness literal, README). Worktree .worktrees/AS-41 is CLEAN (no uncommitted residue). No as41 docker containers survive; the live containers on 8347/8348 were never touched. The lane's last action was tearing down its isolated compose project, and its final line reported that the as41 stripe-mock container had survived a first 'down' and it was retrying — the kill landed during that retry, so cleanup completed by luck rather than by the lane finishing it. Independently verified after the kill: no as41 containers remain.

The stage is NOT complete and the status deliberately stays in_progress — the board tells the truth about interrupted work. Unknown to the orchestrator: whether the suite passed, which acceptance criteria are met, and what remains. The resumer establishes that from the plan, the diff, and a fresh run; nothing here should be taken as a claim that the work is sound.

Deviation on the trial's own clock, recorded rather than hidden: the pre-committed kill point was first-observed-commit + one poll pass = 07:08:35Z. The actual kill was ~13.5 minutes late because the orchestrator's polling cadence was interrupted. The kill mechanism was exercised; the kill-TIMING datum is not a valid measurement of 'kill at first commit' and the spike result must say so rather than re-run for a cleaner number.

lanes-trial: lane spawned — T2 resume. Normal WIP=1 tick under current rules; a fresh implementer sub-agent with no memory of the killed run, briefed only from durable state (task id, plan path, worktree path, branch name, and the kill breadcrumb above). check-resume-preconditions.sh AS-41: examined 4 preconditions, PASS.

Implementation stage resumed after the deliberate mid-flight kill and completed. I was briefed only from durable state and treated the kill comment as a pointer, not a verdict — nothing below is inherited, all of it re-derived.

WHAT I FOUND ALREADY DONE, AND WHETHER IT WAS SOUND. Three commits (8094944, 58c017c, 26a8dfa) carried a COMPLETE implementation against all 16 acceptance criteria. I walked the AC list literally rather than sampling. Diff: 12 files, +1023/-33 — the projected file set exactly (4 new, 8 modified), 1023 vs the §8 projection of ~900 and well under the ~1,100 split line, so no split was triggered. Scope: zero files outside apps/invoicing/, zero .lattice/ files on the branch, neither package.json nor package-lock.json in the diff (zero new dependencies; LOCK_ENTRIES 70 still asserted green). AC 7 verified by grep rather than by reading: `requirementsCurrentlyDue.length === 0` appears exactly ONCE in the whole app, at lib/db/repositories/connected-accounts.js:48 — the AS-41 diff only reads row.ready (2 sites, onboarding.js:88 and :140) and defines no second derivation. AC 13 verified per-commit: each moved literal is in the same commit as the change that moved it (config literals with the config row in 8094944; dependency-policy literals with the three source files in 58c017c; harness literals with connect.test.js in 26a8dfa). The work is sound. I made no code changes and no new commits — there was nothing left to implement.

SUITE, RUN BY ME, ISOLATED PROJECT asc-invoicing-as41 (the live 8347/8348 containers were never touched and are still up and healthy):
- offline `test` service (network_mode: none): 215 tests, 200 pass, 0 fail, 15 skipped, exit 0.
- The 15 skips are exactly the mock gate, enumerated: 12 from stripe-mock.test.js + M1/M2/M3. Zero unexplained skips. M1–M3 report as SKIPPED there, never as passed.
- `contract` service against stripe-mock: 215 tests, 215 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, exit 0. AC 12 holds in both directions.
- V1 instrument check both ways: green normally (exit 0); ASC_SELFTEST_MUTATE=1 → exit 1 with exactly 1 failure, V1 itself.
- Bisect hygiene (my addition): both intermediate commits are independently green in-container — 8094944 and 58c017c each 197 tests / 185 pass / 0 fail / 12 skipped. The branch is bisect-clean.

FALSIFICATION RECIPES (§7 house rules followed: backups in ${TMPDIR}/as41-falsify/ — outside apps/invoicing/ — trap-restore on EXIT, mutation asserted APPLIED before each run, run in-container, tree proven with `git diff --exit-code` after every restore, image rebuilt before the next recipe, and a final rebuild + green re-run at the end).

F1 — strip `platform: true` from the account-CREATE call only.
  assert-applied: 'platform: true' count 4 → 3 (−1 exactly); mutant line confirmed at onboarding.js:99.
  predicted {R3, R12}. OBSERVED {R3, R10, R11, R12} — 4 fail / 196 pass. WIDER THAN PREDICTED; recorded as a finding per §7.
  Why wider, and why it is a strengthening rather than a defect: the custody guard sits UPSTREAM of both the transport and requireKey in AS-38's pipeline (validate→build→guard→requireKey→sign→transport). So R10 (expects 502 from a Stripe 4xx) and R11 (expects 503 from an unconfigured key) both get pre-empted by the 500 custody refusal and trip too. The plan's prediction reasoned only about the tests asserting a 303. Predictions that DID hold: R4/R5/R9 stayed green (their call sites untouched — the narrowness that was the point), and dependency-policy stayed green (the construct still appears in the file).

F2 — hardcode `requirementsCurrentlyDue: []` in readiness.js.
  assert-applied: 'requirementsCurrentlyDue: [],' = 1 hit; 'currently_due' 1 → 0.
  predicted {R1, R6}. OBSERVED {R1, R3, R6} — 3 fail / 197 pass. WIDER: R3 also pins the same due-list literal through the seed-from-create-response path, so the seed is guarded by the same mapping.
  SECOND FINDING, about the plan's stated rationale rather than its set: §7 predicts R6 fails because "the not-ready fixture becomes ready — the trust assertion trips". That is not what happens. The fixture has charges_enabled:false, so AS-39's derivation keeps ready=false whatever the due list. R6 actually trips at connect.test.js:267 on `deepEqual(row.requirementsCurrentlyDue, ['external_account','tos_acceptance.date'])` — the due-list mapping, not the readiness flag. R6 still catches the mutation; the mechanism in the plan is wrong. The TRUST claim is guarded by F4, which is the recipe that actually flips ready.

F3 — disable the row-exists early branch in start(); always take the create path.
  assert-applied: F3-MUTANT marker = 1 hit, original condition = 0 hits.
  predicted {R4, R5}. OBSERVED {R4, R5} — 2 fail / 198 pass. EXACT MATCH.

F4 — replace handleReturn's GET-account + map with a hardcoded all-true ready patch (i.e. an implementation that trusts the return).
  assert-applied: F4-MUTANT = 1 hit; "method: 'GET'" 1 → 0; 'read-account' 0 hits.
  predicted: R6 fails, R7 stays green, M2 fails in the contract service. OBSERVED offline {R6} — 1 fail / 199 pass, R7 green. OBSERVED contract {R6, M2} — 2 fail / 213 pass. EXACT MATCH on all three clauses, including the cross-service one. This is the recipe that proves AC 4: R6, not R7, is the never-trust-the-return guard, and M2 catches it against the mock's own spec-shaped fixture.

F5 — scratch copy of the worktree (never in place), `mv test/connect.test.js test/connect.test.js.bak`.
  assert-applied: `ls test/connect.test.js` failed in the copy; 10 *.test.js remained. Worktree confirmed clean before and after — this recipe never touched it.
  predicted: harness V2 only. OBSERVED {V2} — 1 fail / 184 pass / 12 skipped of 197 tests, message verbatim: "expected exactly 11 test files, found 10: assets.test.js, config.test.js, db.test.js, dependency-policy.test.js, deploy-shape.test.js, harness.test.js, health.test.js, repositories.test.js, stripe-client.test.js, stripe-mock.test.js". EXACT MATCH. (215→197 tests = the 18 connect cases; 15→12 skips = the 3 M-cases.)

F6 — NOT one of the plan's five; added because of a real gap. The dependency-policy concept row `platform Stripe call` is a guard this diff INTRODUCES, and F1 explicitly predicts it stays green — so across F1–F5 it is only ever seen passing, which by our own rule proves nothing. Broke it in the direction it exists to catch: a real (non-comment) `platform: true` in routes/connect.js.
  assert-applied: routes/connect.js 'platform: true' 0 → 1; F6-MUTANT = 1 hit.
  OBSERVED exactly 1 failure — the concept test — 199 pass, message: "platform Stripe call: found in [lib/connect/onboarding.js, routes/connect.js], allowed in exactly [lib/connect/onboarding.js]". §3.6's gate is now proven in both directions.

FINAL STATE after the recipes: tree restored and proven clean (`git diff --exit-code`), images rebuilt, re-run green — offline 200/215 with the same 15 mock-gated skips, contract 215/215. Teardown complete: no as41 containers, no as41 images, no as41 volumes; stripe/stripe-mock:v0.203.0 left pulled; asc-invoicing-web-1 (8348) and asc-chat-server-1 (8347) untouched and healthy throughout; no global prune.

TEST-LITERAL MOVES (§5.4) — all present and green, verified individually: harness EXPECTED_TEST_FILES + connect.test.js at sorted position 3 and cardinality 10→11; dependency-policy source list 26→29 with the three new files in sorted position, new `platform Stripe call` concept row, concept test renamed for AS-41; config SCHEMA.length 9→10, key list gains appBaseUrl after dbPath, INVOICING_-prefixed 8→9, both deepEqual objects updated, plus the new url-type throw cases and the validateResolved case. §5.4.4's deliberately-unmoved set (deploy-shape, health, db, assets, stripe-client, stripe-mock, views.js, package manifests) is untouched and still green — compose.yaml and Dockerfile unchanged as §4 requires.

DEVIATIONS, numbered (all pre-existing in the killed lane's commits; I kept every one and am recording rather than silently ratifying them):
1. handleRefresh short-circuits a ready row to /connect-stripe with zero Stripe calls (tested as R9b). Not in §3.2's route table, which says refresh always mints. Kept: it makes §9 Q1's stated invariant — no code path mints a link for a ready account — enforced rather than assumed, and it is the right answer for a stale bookmark. Q1's own answer is unaffected and still AS-50's to observe.
2. statusFor maps TypeError → 502. Not a row in §3.2's taxonomy table, but required by §3.4 ("TypeError, surfaced as 502 by the route"). Consistent, not an addition.
3. resolveFreelancerId returns null for a REPEATED ?freelancer=a&freelancer=b (Express gives an array). Beyond §3.1's stated signature; hardening, tested in R13.
4. Commit staging: the three source files landed in 58c017c and their tests in 26a8dfa, so 58c017c is green but ships the new source untested. Both intermediates are independently green so the branch is bisect-clean and master is unaffected (merge is --no-ff of the tip). Recorded as hygiene only; not fixable without rewriting history, which the resume was told not to do.
5. §7 predicted failing sets for F1 and F2 are too narrow, and F2's rationale for R6 is wrong (details above). The plan file is board state on master and I do not write to .lattice/ — flagging for the orchestrator/tech lead to correct or annotate. NOTE FOR REVIEW: the correct response is to fix the predictions, NOT to narrow the tests to match them.

BEHAVIOUR WORTH KNOWING, for AS-44's planner and for review: in start(), if connectedAccounts.create succeeds but the subsequent updateReadiness throws for a non-UniqueViolation reason (e.g. the mapper rejects an account shape it does not understand), the error propagates as 502 and the row is left with syncedAt null. The next start finds that row, sees not-ready, and mints a link — self-healing, one row, no extra Stripe account beyond the one already created. Not a defect; recorded so nobody rediscovers it as one.

NAMED RESIDUAL, restated and NOT resolved (AC 14): stripe-mock is stateless and cannot exercise the real hosted-onboarding round trip, and it validates request shapes rather than whether Stripe test mode accepts loopback return/refresh URLs. Both remain AS-50's acceptance run, gated on AS-51. No Stripe account exists, none was opened, no signup of any kind occurred, no board ask was filed, and nothing outside apps/invoicing/ was touched. The only external image used is the already-pulled public stripe-mock, which creates no account, credential, or relationship.

NOTHING LEFT UNDONE within this task's scope. Zero new commits: the implementation was complete when I arrived and the remaining stage work was verification, which produces evidence rather than code.

lanes-trial: lane returned — T2 resume completed. The resumer added no commits: it found the killed stage's implementation already complete and spent the stage verifying it, which is itself the finding (the kill landed after implementation, during container teardown). Sha-stability assertion: all 3 pre-kill commits are unchanged ancestors of the final head 26a8dfa — no rewrite, no duplicate re-application. Lane B's branch and diff are byte-identical to their T1-end state (bc7a39f, 3 files +35/-10), so the surviving lane was unharmed by the kill and the resume.

Review stage: assigning agent:qa-priya. Implementer was Marcus, so implementer != reviewer holds, and this completes the Priya/Ruben split across the trial pair (Ruben took AS-34, passed 7/7, merged at 0b195e5). Still WIP=1: the lanes carve-out is unshipped and its verdict is qualified, so reviews are deliberately not being fanned.
